newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Banque Mediterranee to double capital.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Banque Mediterranee to double capital.

text.p: Banque Mediterrannee, Lebanon's biggest bank, plans to double its capital to about $200 million by the end of the year, chairman Mustafa Razian said on Friday.
"We are planning an additional capital increase prior to the year end which would put us in the level of $200 million," Razian told Reuters in an interview.
"This stems from our strategy for expansion which aims to strengthen the capital base of the bank prior to expanding its activities," he added.
He said his target was to go to $500 million capital by the year 2,000.
Asked about plans for expanding abroad, Razian said: "I would say not Europe. We are talking about regional banking."
Mediterranee, which is 100 percent owned by Lebanon's billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, increased its capital in December 1995 to $100 million from about $47 million.
The bank is listed 59th -- the highest Lebanese bank -- among the top 100 Arab banks in 1995 by Lebanon's Al-Iktissad Wal-Amal (Economy and Business) magazine, up from 80th position in 1994.
